To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) students in an introductory atmospheric science class at the University of Oklahoma held a wide range of ideas about the nature and practice of science, including ideas that are consistent with those held by scientists; and (2) students’ ideas about the nature, practice, and goals of science were related to the number of science classes students had completed prior to the atmospheric science class.

undergraduate atmospheric science students have ideas about science and the scientific process that are similar to ideas about science and scientific processes held by other groups of university students.
the majority of the atmospheric science students in our study held ideas about science that differed from ideas about science that are typically held by university science students.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ideas that undergraduate students hold about the nature of scientific knowledge.
how undergraduate students think about science, and the relationship between these ideas and their previous science coursework.

the ideas that atmospheric science undergraduates have about the nature of scientific knowledge, about scientific inquiry, about the scientific enterprise, and about the role of scientists in society.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of students in the study held a view of science that was consistent with that held by the scientific community, and was consistent with the view held by the National Academy of Science (NAS) (National Academy of Sciences (NAS) 1998) and the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) (American Association for the Advancements of Science (AAASS) 1990).
these undergraduate students have a good understanding of the nature of science and the scientific process.
the majority of these atmospheric science students held ideas about the nature and nature of science that were consistent with those held by the general university science student population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the majority of the students in the sample held a view of science that is consistent with the view of the scientific method that has been promoted in science education for many decades, and that is still promoted today in introductory science textbooks and in science education research.
we found a number of interesting differences between the views of atmospheric science students and those of previous students studied.
students' ideas about science are not a static set of beliefs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
undergraduate students in a science discipline are not homogeneous in their ideas about science and that the nature of their ideas depends on previous coursework.
students' ideas about science are not necessarily the same as those held by the science community.
undergraduate atmospheric science students hold a wide range of ideas about the nature and nature of science.
